entities.name: PMID:25076163
observations: Retrospective University of Rostock analysis of 1,423 venous access port implantations performed 1998–2008; concluded implantation, particularly open access, is an ideal teaching operation within structured surgical training.

Overall complications were 13.8% (early 4.7%, late 9.1%); Seldinger puncture had higher total complications than open cephalic-vein access (14.5% vs 4%, p=0.005). Complications decreased with increasing case experience, although the abstract reports no difference by surgeon experience status.
